title: Chicken and cheese quesadilla
subtitle: Crisp flour tortilla filled with spiced chicken and melted cheese
excerpt: Spiced chicken and melted cheese pressed between two flour tortillas and cooked in a dry pan until crisp and golden. Serve cut into wedges with soured cream, pico de gallo, and a wedge of lime.
sourceNotes: Quesadillas are a staple of Mexican home cooking and Tex-Mex cuisine. Cross-referenced with Rick Bayless, Mexican Kitchen (1996) for technique; the chicken and cheese combination is a standard variation found throughout northern Mexico and the United States.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The spiced chicken can be cooked up to a day ahead and refrigerated. Assemble and grill the quesadillas fresh.

content.text: A good quesadilla needs a very hot dry pan and a cheese that melts well. Mozzarella, Monterey Jack, mild cheddar, or Gruyère all work. The chicken should be seasoned boldly. Do not overfill: the tortilla needs to stay flat enough to press down and cook evenly.

Toss the chicken breast with the cumin, smoked paprika, garlic powder, chilli flakes, oil, and a good pinch of salt. Heat a frying pan over medium-high heat and cook the chicken for 4 to 5 minutes each side until cooked through. Allow to rest for 5 minutes, then shred with two forks or slice thinly.
Wipe out the pan. Heat it over medium-high heat until very hot. Place one tortilla in the dry pan.
Scatter a quarter of the grated cheese over half the tortilla. Add a quarter of the shredded chicken on top of the cheese. Fold the empty half over to make a half-moon.

Press down with a spatula and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until the underside is golden and crisp. Flip and cook for 2 minutes more. The cheese should be fully melted. Remove and cut into 3 wedges. Repeat with the remaining tortillas.
Serve immediately with soured cream, pico de gallo (page reference if available), and lime wedges.

items.symptom: The cheese is not melting before the tortilla burns
items.fix: Reduce heat to medium. The tortilla should colour slowly, giving the cheese time to melt.

items.cause: Too much filling or the pan was not dry and hot
items.fix: Use a thin layer of filling. The pan must be dry and hot; even a little oil makes the tortilla steam instead of crisping.

items.symptom: The quesadilla comes apart when flipped
items.cause: Too much filling or flipped too early
items.fix: Wait until the underside is fully set and golden. Use a wide spatula and flip confidently in one movement.
Check the internal temperature: 74°C is done. Or use thighs instead of breast for more moisture.

content.text: The quesadilla is a corn or flour tortilla folded or pressed with a filling of cheese (and usually something more: meat, beans, vegetables, mushrooms) and cooked until crisp. The cheese quesadilla is eaten across Mexico as a street snack and quick lunch; the chicken and cheese version is associated more specifically with Tex-Mex cooking but is entirely at home in a Mexican kitchen. It is one of the fastest satisfying meals you can make.
